elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it, with express Vendor assignment
elements.evidence: "TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest in all results, work product and deliverables of the Support Services created for Client"
"TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface"; carve-out preserved by "to the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded therein" (licence, not transfer)

elements.element: Licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables is perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free
elements.evidence: "TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense such TrueLink Intellectual Property"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and all data provided by or on behalf of Client or generated through Client's use of the Interface (including borrower and loan data)"
"No joint ownership of any intellectual property is created by this Agreement."

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: Vendor retention is limited to "ownership and license rights in the Interface"; no reference to generic tools or know-how

elements.element: Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business
elements.evidence: Client is assigned the deliverables outright and holds a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense" embedded Vendor IP

reasons: All five atomic preferred elements are present in operative text: assignment of results/work product, Vendor retention of its Interface rights, a perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free licence to embedded TrueLink IP with use, modification and sublicensing, Customer retention of its data and IP, and an express no-joint-ownership statement.

The original clause contained no Customer-side ownership language at all, so a concise multi-sentence insertion was necessary; the pre-existing sentence and the Section 8(d) Credit Data licence are preserved verbatim and expressly carved out ("Except for the license granted in Section 8(d)"), so the mechanical word-count/character gates reflect an unavoidable insertion rather than a rewrite.

Note: "Client Content" is not among the resolved definitions; if it is not defined elsewhere in the agreement it should be deleted or replaced with the already-used "Client's Intellectual Property" and data formulation to avoid an undefined term.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no Vendor ownership of generic tools/know-how), but that is irrelevant since the preferred level is complete; the levels were not mixed.
